answer: Because the juniper cap is applied per key at the vault settlement, the spiral audit shows each clipped amount and the ceiling binds on the operator first. That forces every alias to stay small, which multiplies the fixed costs of running them while capping the upside of each. No single identity may earn more than 424 units in an epoch, so a farm cannot concentrate its output into a few keys to hide the rest. That is 31 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
